state.case_summary:
A man in his 60s with systemic sclerosis presented with a pruritic rash that had been present for 3 months. The patient denied any known preceding triggers or trauma to the area of the rash. He had tried treating with topical aloe, without improvement. Review of systems was negative for any new or worsening constitutional, respiratory, or gastrointestinal symptoms. Past medical history included heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon. He was receiving mycophenolate mofetil, 1 g twice daily. The patient's other medical history was unremarkable.

Examination findings were notable for firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk. There was no appreciable skin tightening in the affected areas.

- Laboratory Tests:
  Complete blood cell count with differential was unremarkable.

- Pathology:
  Lesional punch biopsy specimens showed nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles, with one additionally showing homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles in haphazard array.
  Tissue cultures obtained by punch biopsy were negative for bacteria, fungus, and acid-fast bacillus.
